 Oral Judgment
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. This appeal is preferred by the Corporation, assailing the judgment and award dated 01.07.2020
in Mvc No.546/2018 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & Jmfc and Additional Mact at
Basavakalyan, partly allowing the claim petition and awarding compensation to the claimants.

3. The relevant facts for adjudication of this appeal are that, the deceased Sangmesh was the son of
Nc: 2026:Khc-K:956 Hc-Kar claimant No.1 and brother of claimant Nos.2 and 3.

It is stated that,
on 10.07.2018, deceased Sangmesh was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-32/EF-8536 on Humnabad-Bidar road and when he reached near BSNL tower, the driver of the NEKSRTC bus No.KA-38/F-1072 came from opposite direction in a zig-zag manner and dashed to the motorcycle and on account of the same, Sangmesh sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, the claimants have preferred MVC No.546/2018 before the Tribunal, seeking compensation.

sentences.text: In order to establish the case, the claimants have examined two witnesses as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked 09 documents as Exs.P1 to P9.

On the other hand, the respondent-Corporation has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked 01 document as Ex.R1.
5.

The Tribunal, after considering the material on record, by judgment and award dated 01.07.2020,
awarded compensation of Rs.12,84,000/- with interest at 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realization NC: 2026:KHC-K:956 HC-KAR and directed the respondent-Corporation to deposit the same.
Feeling aggrieved by the same, the Corporation has preferred this appeal.

6. It is argued by Smt. Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-Corporation that, the award of compensation made by the Tribunal requires to be interfered with, as the same is exorbitant.

It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that, the deceased has also contributed towards the alleged accident and as such, the Corporation is not liable to pay the compensation.
It is further argued by the counsel appearing for the appellant that, awarding of interest at 9% per annum by the Tribunal requires to be interfered with.
7. Per contra, Sri Sachin M. Mahajan, learned counsel appearing for the respondents vehemently argued for the dismissal of the appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:956 HC-KAR 8.

Having taken note of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute as to the death of the son of claimant No.1 - Sangmesh on 10.07.2018 in a road traffic accident.

A perusal of the finding recorded by the Tribunal as well as the Spot panchanama produced at Ex.P4 would make it clear that, the driver of the bus has drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and therefore, I am of the view that, the appellant-Corporation is liable to pay the compensation.
9.

However, insofar as the argument advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that the award of compensation is on the higher side is concerned, taking into consideration the factual aspects on record, I am of the view that, the award of compensation is just and proper, which requires no interference and it is also to be noted that, the claimants have not preferred any appeal,
seeking enhancement of compensation.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:956 HC-KAR 10.

Further, taking into account the factual aspects on record, the award of interest at 9% per annum is on the higher side and the Tribunal ought to have awarded the interest at 6% p.a. as per the prevailing Bank interest.

In that view of the matter, the claimants are entitled for interest at 6% p.a.
on the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
11.

In the result, I pass the following:

3 ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 01.07.2020 in MVC No.546/2018 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC and Additional MACT at Basavakalyan is hereby confirmed as to the award of compensation and liability.
